headline: DWP Takes Online Services Offline Following A Cyber Security Incident
seoTitle: DWP Cyber Incident Causes Service Outages
metaDescription: The Department for Work and Pensions has taken some services offline following a cyber incident, with the National Cyber Security Centre assisting.
aiSummaryBullets: The Department for Work and Pensions has taken certain online systems offline following a detected cyber incident.
The National Cyber Security Centre is currently working with the department to address the situation and restore access.
Some benefit claimants have reported issues signing into their Universal Credit accounts as a result of the disruption.
aiContextParagraph: The United Kingdom's Department for Work and Pensions (DWP) has taken a portion of its digital infrastructure offline in response to a cyber security incident. The department is currently collaborating with the National Cyber Security Centre, a branch of GCHQ, to mitigate the impact of the disruption and facilitate the restoration of essential services. While the full extent of the incident remains under assessment, some claimants have reported difficulties accessing their Universal Credit accounts. The situation has prompted public commentary regarding national resilience, with officials noting that the disruption serves as a reminder of the critical importance of protecting public systems. As the DWP works to limit further service issues, authorities are prioritizing the restoration of access for those relying on the department's digital platforms for benefits administration and related support.
whyItIsViral: The incident is viral due to rapid reporting by three independent media outlets and a high velocity of coverage concerning essential government infrastructure.
